title: Gold as an investment — SGBs, gold ETFs and digital gold
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Gold is often used as a hedge against inflation and market falls, but its price can stay flat for years, so it is usually kept to a small slice (commonly 5–10%) of a portfolio, not the whole of it. Paper forms avoid making charges and purity worries: gold ETFs and gold mutual funds trade on exchanges or through fund houses and are SEBI-regulated. Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) gave interest plus gold-price gains but the government has stopped issuing new ones, though existing bonds can still be bought and sold on the exchange. Digital gold sold by apps is not regulated by SEBI or RBI, so understand the risk and the spread between buy and sell price. Physical jewellery is a purchase with making charges and GST, not an investment.
summary_hinglish: Gold inflation aur market girne par support deta hai par kai saal flat bhi reh sakta hai, isliye portfolio ka 5-10% hi rakho. Gold ETF aur gold mutual fund SEBI-regulated hain. Digital gold apps SEBI/RBI regulated nahi hote. Jewellery investment nahi, kharid hai (making charges lagte hain).
summary_hi: सोना महंगाई और बाज़ार गिरने के खिलाफ सहारा देता है पर कई साल सपाट भी रह सकता है, इसलिए पोर्टफोलियो का 5-10% ही रखें। गोल्ड ETF और गोल्ड म्यूचुअल फंड SEBI-नियंत्रित हैं। डिजिटल गोल्ड ऐप SEBI/RBI से नियंत्रित नहीं होते। गहने निवेश नहीं, खरीद हैं।
